statusDetail: The public login surface and adverse conditions were judged, but end-to-end account and commercial flows remain blocked by subscriber number and OTP authentication. No authorized test account was provided.

page.notes: A hash-routed Angular PWA redirects the root to #/login. The public surface is a phone-number login template; account content is authentication-gated.

conditions: activate EN link from Indonesian state

findings.summary: The login experience ignores the requested dark color scheme.
findings.evidence: The default and prefers-color-scheme: dark PNGs have the same 29,984-byte rendering, and the CSS probe found no color-scheme, prefers-color-scheme or light-dark() support.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme: light dark and map surfaces, text, controls and browser chrome to preference-aware tokens using prefers-color-scheme or light-dark().

findings.summary: The language/state navigation has no declared transition treatment.
findings.evidence: Activating the language link triggered a document navigation that closed the inspected target; the CSS probe found no View Transition rules or API usage, so there is no continuity treatment.
findings.suggestedFix: Progressively enhance language and route changes with same-document or cross-document View Transitions, while preserving the reduced-motion behavior already present.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus is invisible and language targets are too small.
findings.evidence: The live focus probe found outline-style none and no box shadow on the phone field. EN and ID measure only 18x21 and 15x21 CSS pixels, below the 44x44 target guidance.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a high-contrast :focus-visible indicator and enlarge the clickable language controls to at least 44x44 CSS pixels without shrinking their visible labels.

findings.summary: Invalid phone input gives no actionable state or accessible error.
findings.evidence: After entering and blurring “123”, native validity still reported valid, Continue remained disabled, no role=alert or visible error appeared, and aria-invalid was absent.
findings.suggestedFix: Validate after interaction, show a specific correction message, set aria-invalid, associate the message with aria-describedby, and announce it in a live region.

findings.summary: The throttled Largest Contentful Paint is far outside the good range.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP at 9.18 seconds with performance score 0.74. The raw trace measured LCP at 4.02 seconds, so both miss the 2.5-second good threshold.
findings.suggestedFix: Profile the LCP element and its dependency chain, prioritize only its required resources, and defer non-critical application code until after the login form is visible.

findings.summary: The small login screen downloads a heavy, inefficient application payload.
findings.evidence: The HAR recorded 1.93 MB over 17 requests, including 1.61 MB of scripts and 211 KB of fonts. The 1.18 MB vendor bundle dominates the load, and large document/JS responses are uncompressed.
findings.suggestedFix: Enable Brotli compression, use immutable long-lived caching for hashed assets, subset and preload only the needed font, and split the authentication route from the main application dependency graph.

findings.summary: Most JavaScript and CSS shipped to the login route is unused.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 1,042 KiB unused JavaScript and 69 KiB unused CSS; vendor is 63% unused, main 79%, and scripts 85%.
findings.suggestedFix: Route-split the login experience, remove duplicate legacy or unconditional dependencies, tree-shake production bundles, and load account-only features conditionally after authentication.

findings.summary: Decorative images expose punctuation as alternative text.
findings.evidence: The image audit and rendered DOM show both the 1x1 pixel and phone-prefix SVG use alt=".". Screen readers may announce meaningless punctuation.
findings.suggestedFix: Use alt="" for decorative images and keep meaningful icon information in a concise accessible name on the associated control.

findings.summary: Four visible text elements fail WCAG AA contrast.
findings.evidence: axe measured four visible text failures: language/sign-up text at 4.31:1 and the phone label/helper at 3.49:1 against white.
findings.suggestedFix: Darken the gray and red text tokens to reach at least 4.5:1 against white in all states, then re-run automated and visual contrast checks.

findings.summary: The login document lacks semantic structure and visible focus.
findings.evidence: axe found no main landmark, no h1, invalid h2-to-h5 order and content outside landmarks; the focus probe found no visible outline or shadow.
findings.suggestedFix: Wrap the primary form in main, use one descriptive h1 with sequential headings, and add a persistent high-contrast :focus-visible style.

findings.summary: Supporting text is visually weak at small sizes.
findings.evidence: The mobile screenshot shows 12px gray verification copy; axe measured it at only 3.49:1 against white.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a legible minimum body/helper size with comfortable line height, stronger contrast and wrapping that remains readable at narrow widths.

findings.summary: The viewport explicitly prevents user zoom.
findings.evidence: The live viewport meta contains user-scalable=no and maximum-scale=1.0. axe classifies this as a critical accessibility failure.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove user-scalable=no and maximum-scale=1.0, retain width=device-width and initial-scale=1, and verify reflow at 200% to 400% zoom.

findings.summary: A production script throws an uncaught Swiper reference error.
findings.evidence: Current Lighthouse console capture reports ReferenceError: Swiper is not defined at scripts.e33c1cecaaf7f13ff778.js:2:166840.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove the stale initializer or conditionally load and initialize Swiper only after its dependency is available.

findings.summary: An inline SVG image has no intrinsic dimensions.
findings.evidence: The images primitive found the phone-prefix SVG renders at 28x35 without width/height attributes; layout captures show small non-zero CLS.
findings.suggestedFix: Add width and height attributes, or an aspect-ratio, matching the rendered prefix icon dimensions so space is reserved before it loads.

findings.summary: Large production JavaScript has no source map.
findings.evidence: Current Lighthouse reports that the 1.18 MB first-party vendor bundle has no valid source map.
findings.suggestedFix: Publish protected production source maps to the error-monitoring pipeline or serve valid maps where policy allows, and keep release artifacts aligned.

findings.summary: Navigation controls are not crawlable links and robots.txt is missing.
findings.evidence: The only anchors, EN and ID, use href="javascript:void()". /robots.txt returns HTTP storage NoSuchKey XML rather than a robots policy.
findings.suggestedFix: Use real URLs for language variants and serve a valid robots.txt that explicitly states crawl policy and points to the sitemap.

findings.summary: Public indexing signals are incomplete.
findings.evidence: The HTTP 200 login document has no canonical or hreflang links; robots.txt and sitemap.xml return NoSuchKey XML responses.
findings.suggestedFix: Add an absolute canonical URL, hreflang links for Indonesian and English variants, and a sitemap consistent with robots policy.

findings.summary: The authentication client lacks CSP and embeds a reusable authorization value in its public bundle.
findings.evidence: The header audit found no Content-Security-Policy. The redacted bundle context contains static SERVICEKEY and hdrAuthorization values; the Google API key is public client configuration, but API authorization must not rely on reusable values shipped to every browser.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a nonce- or hash-based CSP and remove trust in static client credentials. Enforce authorization at the server with short-lived, user-bound tokens and rotate the exposed value if it grants access.

findings.summary: The account entry offers phone OTP only, with no phishing-resistant option.
findings.evidence: The public login form requests a phone number for OTP and no permission prompt appears on load. No passkey or WebAuthn affordance is exposed on this entry path.
findings.suggestedFix: Offer passkey sign-in and registration alongside the existing recovery path, with conditional mediation where supported.

findings.summary: Several browser-enforced defensive policies are absent.
findings.evidence: HSTS, nosniff and SAMEORIGIN are present; CSP, Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy are absent.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a restrictive CSP with frame-ancestors, a privacy-preserving Referrer-Policy and a least-privilege Permissions-Policy.

findings.summary: The login flow is unusable without JavaScript.
findings.evidence: The JavaScript-disabled screenshot shows only “Please enable JavaScript to continue using this application.” Raw-to-rendered content coverage is 6%.
findings.suggestedFix: Server-render the login form and essential instructions, use a real form action for the core step, then enhance validation and transitions with JavaScript.

findings.summary: Unknown paths expose a raw storage error with no recovery.
findings.evidence: Requesting /this-route-does-not-exist returns HTTP 404 with raw NoSuchKey XML and no navigation, retry or link back to login.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve an intentional 404 page with a clear explanation and link back to the login or help path; use the same recoverable pattern for API and timeout errors.

findings.summary: Language metadata and CSS do not match the visible locale or support bidirectional layout.
findings.evidence: The selected visible content is Indonesian while html lang remains en. The CSS probe found zero logical-property matches and roughly 900 physical left/right declarations.
findings.suggestedFix: Set html lang dynamically to id or en, declare direction where needed, and migrate layout declarations to logical properties so translated and RTL content can reflow.

findings.summary: The phone field disables useful browser input assistance.
findings.evidence: The live sign-in telephone input explicitly sets autocomplete="off".
findings.suggestedFix: Use the appropriate tel autocomplete token and inputmode so users can safely reuse stored contact/sign-in information rather than retyping it.
